taxonomic_note: Accepted species; Texas-native at the state level but fails the project's current target-zone native threshold.
look_here_first: Look at the leaf and climbing organ together: crossvine usually has two broad leaflets, with the third leaflet position modified into a branched tendril ending in adhesive pads.

project_inclusion.range_basis: USDA-derived Texas county/native-status data provide only Bandera inside the current target zone. Travis occurrences are explicitly documented as cultivated in the deep review.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Broad ecoregion presence and cultivated Hill Country records are not converted into exact native counties.

best_field_traits: evergreen to semi-evergreen woody climbing vine
third leaflet position modified into a branched tendril
tendril branches end in adhesive discs/pads
leaflets broad, glossy and mostly entire
showy orange-red to reddish/yellow trumpet-shaped flowers
long flattened 2-valved capsule with winged seeds
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The two-leaflet-plus-tendril architecture is the fastest way to separate crossvine from trumpet creeper.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Trumpet creeper has 7–11 serrated leaflets and aerial rootlets. Catclaw vine has claw-like hooks at the tendril tips. Coral honeysuckle has simple leaves and berries.
